problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=3 and h a smooth positive Hermitian form. Fix a smooth strictly positive probability dV, use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and use genuine canonical h-plurisubharmonic representatives. Define v_minus(h)=inf{integral_X(h+dd^c u)^n:u is bounded and h-psh}; assume v_minus(h)=0. This is the bounded-potential mass infimum, not the fixed-density Gauduchon volume.
For nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), b_h(f)>=0 is the maximal coefficient of a genuine subsolution MA_h^ext(u)>=b_h(f)f dV, equivalently the limit of continuous-equation normalization scalars of min(f,k). The extended non-pluripolar measure is defined by finite-level truncation and can have infinite total mass.
For a measurable real or complex root p in Ln(dV), set rho_h(p)=b_h(|p|^n)^(-1/n), taking rho_h(0)=0 and infinite value for a zero threshold. Equivalently rho_h(p)=sup_T integral_X |p| k_T dV, with T smooth positive (n-1,n-1), dd^c T=0, integral_X h wedge T=1, T=gamma^(n-1), and k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n). The supremum uses all such tests. Set D_h={p in Ln:rho_h(p)<infinity} with norm ||p||_Ln+rho_h(p), and D_h^0 the closure of bounded measurable roots in that norm.
Original S04 has two questions. First, must D_h^0=D_h when v_minus(h)=0? Equivalently must every finite positive-threshold root p satisfy rho_h(|p| 1_{|p|>K})->0 as K tends to infinity, or can a positive-threshold root have nonvanishing uniform tails? Second, do these uniform root tails suffice for the exact finite-mass equation in P07: for nonzero f>=0 in L1 with b_h(f)>0 and f^(1/n) in D_h^0, does some genuine h-psh u satisfy MA_h^ext(u)=b_h(f) f dV, in a rigorously specified natural singularity or envelope class?
Known background: p in D_h^0 iff the displayed root-tail norm tends to zero, equivalently norm convergence under every dominated perturbation tending to zero in smooth-volume measure. Smooth roots are dense in D_h^0, which contains Lr for r>n. At positive lower mass both spaces equal Ln, so that regime does not resolve this question. Uniform root tails give scalar continuity, dual attainment and error moduli for exponential approximations. They do not in the known argument supply capacity compactness or a smaller-background envelope for potentials. Every positive threshold is attained by a subsolution, possibly with excess or infinite mass; Lp densities for p>1 have a continuous exact solution. The general L1 exact equation at zero lower mass remains open. An abstract Banach-function-space example or failure of an endpoint bound does not exhibit a root on an actual compact Hermitian manifold. No candidate root, geometry, conclusion or proof is supplied.
completionCriteria: Resolve either original question in full by a complete proof or an actual compact Hermitian counterexample. For the first negative answer give explicit X,h,dV,p with v_minus(h)=0, p in Ln, finite rho_h(p) and a strictly positive lower limit for its tail norms, proving all of these from the full test formula or genuine subsolutions. For a positive answer prove every such root is order-continuous without imposing positive lower mass or stronger density integrability. For the second question retain the exact threshold and finite prescribed measure, specify the equation class, and prove the required compactness/product passage; scalar and measure convergence alone do not suffice. Distinguish the two questions if only one is answered, and do not infer whole-family potential uniqueness. Verify pivotal external statements at primary sources and independently reconstruct the complete result.
